## Objective

This vignette demonstrates how to locate, read, summarize, and visualize the
sample boundary and Digital Terrain Model distributed with `dem30mDownloadR`. The example uses
only package-internal files resolved with `system.file()`, so it can be run
after installation on another machine.

## Load packages

```{r packages}
library(dem30mDownloadR)
library(sf)
library(terra)
```

## Locate the package data

```{r locate-data}
dem_path <- system.file(
  "extdata", "GEDTM30_API_original.tif",
  package = "dem30mDownloadR"
)
boundary_path <- system.file(
  "extdata", "boundary_buffer.geojson",
  package = "dem30mDownloadR"
)

stopifnot(nzchar(dem_path), nzchar(boundary_path))
c(dem = dem_path, boundary = boundary_path)
```

## Read and inspect the data

```{r read-data}
dem <- rast(dem_path)
boundary <- st_read(boundary_path, quiet = TRUE)
boundary_dem <- st_transform(boundary, crs(dem))

dem
```

The DTM is a one-band bare-earth elevation raster. We next calculate basic summary
statistics in metres:

```{r summary}
values <- values(dem, mat = FALSE)
summary_table <- data.frame(
  statistic = c("Minimum", "Mean", "Median", "Maximum"),
  elevation_m = c(
    min(values, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean(values, na.rm = TRUE),
    median(values, na.rm = TRUE),
    max(values, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
)
summary_table
```

The raster extent and boundary should overlap. If they do not, loading or
coordinate-system transformation is incorrect:

```{r overlap}
dem_extent <- ext(dem)
dem_bbox_coordinates <- rbind(
  c(dem_extent[1], dem_extent[3]),
  c(dem_extent[2], dem_extent[3]),
  c(dem_extent[2], dem_extent[4]),
  c(dem_extent[1], dem_extent[4]),
  c(dem_extent[1], dem_extent[3])
)
dem_bbox_sf <- st_sfc(
  st_polygon(list(dem_bbox_coordinates)),
  crs = 4326
)

boundary_in_dem <- st_intersects(
  dem_bbox_sf,
  boundary_dem,
  sparse = FALSE
)[1, 1]

boundary_in_dem
```

## Visualize elevation

The displayed color range uses the observed minimum and maximum so that the
full elevation contrast is preserved.

```{r dem-map, fig.alt="Map of the SCBI GEDTM30 sample DTM with a study-area boundary and 50 metre contours."}
elevation_range <- range(values, na.rm = TRUE)
colors <- colorRampPalette(c(
  "#5B1A18", "#A52A2A", "#E66101", "#FDB863",
  "#FFFFBF", "#A6D96A", "#1A9850", "#006837"
))(100)

plot(
  dem,
  col = colors,
  zlim = elevation_range,
  axes = TRUE,
  main = "SCBI GEDTM30 30 m DTM",
  xlab = "Longitude",
  ylab = "Latitude",
  plg = list(title = "Elevation\n(m)")
)

contours <- as.contour(dem, levels = seq(250, 650, by = 50))
plot(contours, add = TRUE, col = "#333333", lwd = 0.7)
plot(boundary_dem, add = TRUE, col = NA, border = "#000000", lwd = 2)
legend(
  "bottomleft",
  legend = c("Boundary", "50 m contours"),
  col = c("#000000", "#333333"),
  lwd = c(2, 1),
  bty = "n"
)
```

## Interpretation

The statistics and map show the spatial distribution of elevation within the
sample area. These values are intended to demonstrate package data access and
visualization; they are not a substitute for a complete terrain or ecological
analysis.
